Set up & run

Configuration

Every setting lives in .sdlc/config.json. You can edit it by hand. This page covers the keys a new adopter needs; the full list is in the configuration reference linked at the bottom.

In plain words

The config file is a plain text file of switches. Sigma ships with the risky ones off: it will not merge anything by itself, it spends within a ceiling, and it holds work when your machine is short of memory. You turn a switch on when you have a reason. Change one at a time, then run /sigma-doctor to see what is on.

Editing by hand

  • It is JSON. A stray comma breaks it, so keep the file valid after every edit.
  • Keys that start with an underscore are notes written by the scaffold. Leave them.
  • When .sdlc/config.json and the prose in project.md disagree, the config wins.
  • A value that is the wrong type or out of range is usually read as the default, with a note. That is forgiving but quiet: check the result with /sigma-doctor.
  • An update never rewrites the file. A block added by a later release has to be copied in from the template in the installed plugin.
{
  "discovery": { "source": "github", "order": "priority" },
  "verify":    { "command": "your test command", "enforce": true },
  "work":      { "enabled": true, "auto_merge": "off", "require_review": "changes" },
  "budget":    { "max_iterations": 20, "max_minutes": 480, "max_tokens": 100000000 },
  "handoff":   { "enabled": true, "after_goals": 20 }
}

This is a trimmed excerpt using the scaffold's own values, not the whole file. verify.command is yours; init records it when you confirm a detected command.

Where goals come from

KeyScaffoldedWhat it does and when to change it
discovery.sourcelocal-goals; init chooses github when origin is a GitHub repositorylocal-goals reads files in .sdlc/goals/. github reads issues labelled sdlc:goal and needs gh. Change it only to move the backlog; the loop runs the same either way.
discovery.orderprioritypriority sorts by the priority:P0 to P4 label (or the priority: key in a goal file), oldest first within a tier; a goal with no priority sorts last. created is strict oldest-first.

Proof: the verify command

KeyScaffoldedWhat it does and when to change it
verify.commandemptyThe command that proves a goal's change works. Set it by confirming a candidate at init, or later with the verify gesture from the init output. A literal command is never taken from a flag.
verify.enforcefalse, turned on when a command is confirmedOn: record done and a merge are refused without fresh passing evidence from this run. Never turn it on with an empty command: every done would be refused.
verify.known_flakesabsentA person-approved, time-limited list of tests allowed to fail a full verify. Nothing adds an entry automatically.

Landing: pull requests and merging

KeyScaffoldedWhat it does and when to change it
work.enabledtrueOne worktree, branch and pull request per goal. Your own checkout never moves. Off means the loop edits the checkout directly (also the result of --local-only).
work.auto_merge"off"off never merges; it leaves the pull request. protected merges only where the base branch requires checks or reviews. always merges any clean and safe pull request, but still stops where protection could not be read. Turn on protected only after you have set branch protection. See Trust and limits.
work.require_review"changes"changes parks on a request-changes review or an unresolved thread. approval also requires an approval. off relies on branch protection alone.
work.ci_requiredtruefalse stops waiting on non-required checks, for teams whose real CI runs elsewhere. A check the base branch requires still blocks.
work.max_review_cycles3How many review-to-fix rounds before the goal is parked.
followups.mode, followups.max_added_slicesin-goal, 10A follow-up found in a goal's own feature joins that goal as a slice; a separate goal is filed only for another feature or once the goal holds the cap. The cap is a whole number of at least 1; anything else reads as 10, never unlimited. "file" opts back out to one goal per follow-up.

There is no setting for unreadable branch protection, and none is needed: when protection cannot be read, the merge is held. See Trust and limits.

Gates and review

KeyScaffoldedWhat it does and when to change it
gates.phase_recordonrecord done and a merge are refused unless every phase is on record, including an approved plan-review.
gates.plan_reviewoffAlso refuses the pull-request push without an approving plan-review for the exact plan. Turn on when you want it enforced at the push, not only at done.
gates.hard_plan_gateoffRefuses the pull-request push for a goal with no plan, and on Claude Code the edit itself.
review.independenttrueAsks for a fresh, author-blind reviewer. This is an instruction to the agent; no code proves the maker did not influence the reviewer.
goal_readiness.modewarnwarn prints the sections a goal lacks and proceeds. require parks it. off checks nothing.

Budgets and hand-off

KeyScaffoldedWhat it does and when to change it
budget.max_iterations20Goals per session.
budget.max_minutes480Wall-clock minutes from the session's own start.
budget.max_tokens100000000Priced Claude-equivalent tokens, counted from phases with a full price.
budget.max_codex_raw_tokens0 (off)Measured Codex input plus output tokens. A phase-boundary admission stop, not a quota or a bill.
handoff.after_goals20The orchestrating session stops claiming after this many goals and hands off to a fresh one, so its context does not grow across a long drain.
parallel.goals.enabled, max_concurrentoff, 3Several backlog goals at once, one worktree and pull request each. Size max_concurrent to memory, not to the number of open issues.

A budget enforces only when set to a positive number. Each belongs to the session that started it, so several sessions side by side can together spend several times one ceiling. Size the ceilings with that in mind.

Batches and cloud sessions

The settings for these are in the tables above (followups.*, verify.known_flakes) and work.checkpoint_prefix (default empty: the goal branch itself). How they behave is on Running many goals and Cloud sessions.

The resource guard

Every resource.* key is scaffolded as null, which means derived from this machine. Leave them null unless a hold is wrong for your machine.

KeyDerived defaultMeaning
resource.modeenforceobserve logs the hold it would make and admits; off skips the check. The environment variable SIGMA_RESOURCE_MODE overrides the key everywhere.
resource.reserve_fraction0.20 of memoryMemory kept free for the machine.
resource.max_share_fraction0.60 of memoryMost memory all sessions together may lease.
resource.cpu_reserve_coresone eighth of cores, at least 1Cores kept free.
resource.max_goals, max_verify_workersno extra capHard caps on concurrent goals and verify workers.

Not calibrated: the fractions are policy ratios, not yet fitted to a real exhaustion. Two recorded runs (macOS, and Linux in a 2 GiB container) fixed none of them. See Running unattended.

Optional features

KeyScaffoldedTurn it on when
ledger.enabledundecided, reads as offMore than one person runs the loop. See As a team.
action_log.enabledtrueKeep on. It is the local trace that /sigma-log reads; it never leaves your machine.
slack_commands.enabledfalseYou have done the manual Slack setup. See From Slack.
model_selection"auto" (the code default is off; the scaffold template writes auto)You want a model tier chosen per goal rather than one model for everything. Conflicts resolve upward.
agent_watch.enabledfalseYou want a notice when a claimed goal's process has died. Needs the ledger.
upkeep.enabledfalseYou run long-lived unit branches and want them kept rebased. Read the upkeep guide first.
backlog_check.enabledfalseYou want duplicate or obsolete goals parked before any tokens are spent.
Technical detail

Defaults here are what the scaffold writes, read from its template; the code default for an absent key can differ (for example the action log is off in code when the key is absent). The full reference, including quota, sweep, known-flake and per-category autonomy keys, is configuration. What enforces each setting, and on which host, is enforcement. Environment variables worth knowing: SIGMA_RESOURCE_MODE, SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SIGMA_SLACK_BOT_SOCKET_TOKEN (secrets stay in the environment, never in the file), and the operator-set verify approval for cloud environments.
